svg.text: FIG 04: RECIPROCITY THEOREM, DUAL TRANSFER FUNCTIONS & 30-SECOND T-NETWORK SYNTHESIS
4 Mandatory Axioms • Transfer Admittance & Impedance Invariance • Superposition + Reciprocity Synthesis • Faculty 30-Sec T-Model Shortcut

g.text: 1. Reciprocity Axioms & Principles
The Reciprocity Theorem Principle
In any linear, bilateral, time-invariant, passive network with a SINGLE excitation,
the ratio of the response at branch 2 to the excitation at branch 1 remains
IDENTICAL if the positions of excitation and response are interchanged!
Transfer Ratio Invariance: [Response / Excitation] ≡ const
• Interchanging excitation and response produces the EXACT SAME numerical ratio.
• Crucial: Reference polarities and meter orientations must be strictly preserved.
THE 4 MANDATORY CONDITIONS OF RECIPROCITY
Reciprocity holds IF AND ONLY IF all 4 conditions are simultaneously satisfied:
1. Linear Elements Only:
R, L, C elements must be linear (no diodes, saturation, or clipping).
2. Bilateral Elements Only:
Impedance must be identical in both directions of current flow.
3. Passive Network (Zero Independent Sources):
Network must not contain any other internal independent sources or initial energy.
4. ZERO DEPENDENT SOURCES (The Ultimate Trap!):
Active controlled sources (VCVS, VCCS, CCVS, CCCS), Op-Amps, BJTs, and FETs
DESTROY RECIPROCITY! Networks with dependent sources are NON-RECIPROCAL.
(Special non-reciprocal microwave elements: Gyrators, Circulators, Isolators).
Two-Port Matrix Reciprocity Criteria
In 2-port network parameter formulations, reciprocity manifests as symmetry:
Impedance [Z] Parameters:
Z₁₂ = Z₂₁ (Symmetric Z-Matrix: Z = Zᵀ)
Admittance [Y] Parameters:
Y₁₂ = Y₂₁ (Symmetric Y-Matrix: Y = Yᵀ)
Transmission (ABCD) Parameters:
A · D - B · C = 1 (Unit Determinant: det[T] = 1)
Hybrid [h] and Inverse Hybrid [g] Parameters:
h₁₂ = -h₂₁ and g₁₂ = -g₂₁ (Anti-Symmetric Off-Diagonals!)
Energy & Symmetry Foundations
• Reciprocity arises from the fundamental symmetry of Maxwell's wave equations
and Onsager's reciprocal relations for microscopic thermodynamics.
Quasi-Tellegen Topological Link:
Applying Quasi-Tellegen theorem to two network states N and N' on same graph:
∑ v_k · i_k' = 0 and ∑ v_k' · i_k = 0
For linear bilateral branches, v_k i_k' = (i_k Z_k) i_k' = i_k' Z_k i_k = v_k' i_k.
Subtracting the two sums leaves only port excitations:
V₁ I₁' + V₂ I₂' = V₁' I₁ + V₂' I₂ ⟹ Proves Reciprocity!
Topological proof holds for ANY arbitrary planar or non-planar graph!
2. Dual Forms of Reciprocity
FORM 1: Transfer Admittance Reciprocity (V → I)
Voltage Excitation & Short-Circuit Current Response:
• State 1: Connect ideal voltage source V₁ at Port 1; short-circuit Port 2
and measure short-circuit current I₂.
• State 2: Connect ideal voltage source V₂' at Port 2; short-circuit Port 1
and measure short-circuit current I₁'.
Reciprocal Relation:
I₂ / V₁ = I₁' / V₂' [Unit: Siemens (S = Ω⁻¹)]
If source voltages are identical (V₁ = V₂'): Then I₂ = I₁' exactly!
Ideal Ammeter: Has R_A = 0 Ω, so connecting an ideal ammeter shorts the branch.
FORM 2: Transfer Impedance Reciprocity (I → V)
Current Excitation & Open-Circuit Voltage Response:
• State 1: Inject ideal current source I₁ at Port 1; open-circuit Port 2
and measure open-circuit voltage V₂.
• State 2: Inject ideal current source I₂' at Port 2; open-circuit Port 1
and measure open-circuit voltage V₁'.
Reciprocal Relation:
V₂ / I₁ = V₁' / I₂' [Unit: Ohms (Ω)]
If source currents are identical (I₁ = I₂'): Then V₂ = V₁' exactly!
Ideal Voltmeter: Has R_v = ∞ Ω, so connecting an ideal voltmeter opens the branch.
THE FATAL CROSS-FORM TRAP: V/V and I/I DO NOT EQUATE!
Students frequently interchange Voltage Excitation with Voltage Response:
V₂ / V₁ ≠ V₁' / V₂' (Voltage Transfer Ratio FAILS!)
I₂ / I₁ ≠ I₁' / I₂' (Current Transfer Ratio FAILS!)
Why Dimensionless Ratios Fail:
• Voltage gain V₂/V₁ is dimensionless; it depends on impedance levels at each port.
• A step-up transformer has V₂/V₁ = N₂/N₁ > 1, but backwards V₁'/V₂' = N₁/N₂ < 1!
GOLDEN RULE: Reciprocity ONLY equates Transfer Admittance (I/V) or
Transfer Impedance (V/I). Dimensionless transfer gains are NOT invariant!
Meter Sign Conventions & Reference Arrows
When interchanging sources and meters:
• The positive terminal of the source in the new position must match the
direction of the arrow of the response current in the original position!
• If current arrow pointed INTO terminal B originally, the voltage source positive
terminal must face OUT of terminal B when relocated.
• Reversing meter leads introduces a fatal -1 sign error into numerical answers.
Diagnostic Rule: Trace complete traversal loop to verify matching orientations!
3. Faculty 30-Sec T-Network Shortcut
THE REVOLUTIONARY T-NETWORK EQUIVALENCE SHORTCUT
Conventional Method: Solving combined Reciprocity + Superposition problems
takes 10–15 minutes of tedious multi-mesh matrix inversions and phasor algebra.
The PrepFusion Faculty Shortcut:
ANY linear, passive, reciprocal 2-port black box can be EXACTLY synthesized
as a simple 3-resistor T-Network (R_a, R_b, R_c) with IDENTICAL terminal behavior!
Once R_a, R_b, R_c are found, solve ANY new load in 30 seconds via KVL!
Step-by-Step T-Network Synthesis Architecture
T-Network Topology:
Port 1 (Terminals 1-1') ──[ R_a ]──●──[ R_b ]── Port 2 (Terminals 2-2')
[ R_c ]
Extracting R_a, R_b, R_c from 2 Experimental Test States:
Test Case 1: Connect 10 V at Port 1; Port 2 is shorted with measured I₂ = 2 A.
Loop 1 KVL: 10 V = I₁ · (R_a + R_c) - 2 A · R_c
Loop 2 KVL: 0 V = -I₁ · R_c + 2 A · (R_b + R_c)
Test Case 2: Connect 20 V at Port 2; Port 1 is open with measured V₁ = 5 V.
Voltage Divider across R_c: V₁ = 20 V · [ R_c / (R_b + R_c) ] = 5 V
⟹ (R_b + R_c) / R_c = 4 ⟹ R_b = 3 R_c
Substituting into Case 1 gives exact numerical values in 3 lines:
Solving the Target Problem in 10 Seconds
Target Question: "If Port 1 is connected to 50 V and Port 2 is connected to a 10 Ω
load resistor, find current through the 10 Ω load."
Using our synthesized T-model with R_L = 10 Ω connected at Port 2:
Total resistance seen at Port 1: R_in = R_a + [ R_c ∥ (R_b + R_L) ]
Input current: I₁ = 50 V / 3.4375 Ω = 14.545 A
Why Every GATE Titan Memorizes This Method:
1. Eliminates abstract two-port reciprocal matrix equations.
2. Visualizes the black-box as a simple 2-mesh resistive circuit.
3. Works equally for any new combination of sources and loads at either port!
4. Multi-Source Reciprocity & Traps
Combining Reciprocity with Superposition
When multiple sources act simultaneously across a reciprocal network:
Problem: Sources V₁ at Port 1 and V₂ at Port 2 drive current I_x in branch x.
The 3-Step Solution Flow:
1. Use Reciprocity to find transfer admittance of source 1: y_x1 = I_x' / V₁.
2. Use Reciprocity to find transfer admittance of source 2: y_x2 = I_x'' / V₂.
3. Superpose the two partial currents algebraically:
I_x,total = y_x1 · V₁ + y_x2 · V₂
Guaranteed valid because the network is linear and bilateral!
Fast Shunt-Only Synthesis Example
A reciprocal network has symmetrical ports. Given experimental data:
When 10 V is connected at Port 1, short-circuit current at Port 2 is I₂ = 5 A.
Synthesizing as a Single Shunt Resistor R_sh:
Transfer admittance: Y₂₁ = I₂ / V₁ = 5 A / 10 V = 0.5 S ⟹ Transfer Z = 2 Ω.
If internal series arms R_a = R_b = 0 Ω, then shunt arm R_c = 2 Ω:
Target Response:
If a 15 V source is connected at Port 2 with a 3 Ω resistor at Port 1:
Solved in 2 lines with 100% mathematical precision.
Common Reciprocity Misconceptions in GATE
Misconception 1: "Reciprocity holds for power transfer."
REALITY: Absolutely FALSE! Power transfer is NOT reciprocal: P₁₂ ≠ P₂₁.
Misconception 2: "Can apply reciprocity to circuits with op-amps."
REALITY: Op-amps have unilateral forward gain A → ∞, non-reciprocal!
Misconception 3: "Internal mesh currents remain identical when swapped."
REALITY: ONLY the specific transfer port response is invariant. Internal branch
voltages and currents completely change when source is moved!
Reciprocity Exam Verification Checklist
✓ Are all resistors, inductors, and capacitors linear and bilateral?
✓ Are there ZERO controlled sources (VCVS, VCCS, CCVS, CCCS)?
✓ Are there ZERO independent sources other than the test excitation?
✓ Did you equate Transfer Admittance (I/V) or Transfer Impedance (V/I)?
✓ Did you avoid the dimensionless V/V and I/I transfer gain trap?
If all boxes checked: Solution is guaranteed mathematically flawless!
